scenarios.name: CHP only
scenarios.description: No upgrading: the whole gas output goes to the engine, and what it cannot take is flared.

scenarios.name: Biomethane only
scenarios.description: No CHP: all the gas is upgraded and injected. The digester heat then has to come from the boiler.

scenarios.name: Hybrid by price
scenarios.description: Both units run, but each stands down when the other use of a cubic metre of methane is worth more -- the dispatch is led by the hourly electricity price.

scenarios.name: Grass instead of maize
scenarios.description: The second feedstock mix: grass silage instead of maize -- a lower yield and a slower release, at a lower price.

schedules.name: Bio Delivery campaign

exceptions.description: Outside the maize campaign: no maize deliveries

schedules.description: The maize campaign as REAL WEEKS: deliveries every day from the harvest until the dated exception closes the campaign eight weeks later (PHASE4 T10).

schedules.name: Bio CHP maintenance
schedules.description: A MONTHLY service day, so it stays a points schedule: a weekday grid says weeks, not months (ARCHITECTURE D81).

timeseries_inputs.name: Bio feed continuous
timeseries_inputs.description: A flat multiplier: the recipe is fed evenly around the clock.

timeseries_inputs.name: Bio feed 8 batches
timeseries_inputs.description: A batch feeder: 3.0 for eight hours from 06:00, 0 for the rest of the day. Its daily mean is 1, so the daily amount is still the recipe.

timeseries_inputs.name: Bio power price
timeseries_inputs.description: SYNTHETIC hourly day-ahead price, EUR/kWh: one weekly pattern (a morning and an evening peak, 10% lower at the weekend) repeated over the year. It is not a real market series -- replace it with one before a price-led dispatch conclusion is quoted.

timeseries_inputs.name: Bio biomethane price
timeseries_inputs.description: A flat multiplier of 1.0 on the biomethane price. Replace the values for an indexed or seasonal price.

timeseries_inputs.name: Bio spreading windows
timeseries_inputs.description: Spreading allowed (1) or closed (0), one value per REAL WEEK from the maize harvest on Monday 7 September 2026: the autumn window, the winter closure and the spring reopening are dates, not offsets. Illustrative -- replace it with your own regulation.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg load profile
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative household demand, normalised to its evening peak, one value per hour of the day (about 9 times the peak in kWh per day).

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg tariff
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative time-of-use import price, EUR/kWh, by hour of the day.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg flat tariff
timeseries_inputs.description: A flat import price, EUR/kWh: one value, held for the whole run.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg grid intensity
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative grid carbon intensity, kg CO2e per kWh, by hour of the day: cleaner around midday, dirtier at the evening peak.

levels.name: Bio Feed store
levels.description: Feedstock in store, tonnes (solid) or cubic metres (liquid). Unmet is the feeding shortfall: what the feeder asked for and the store could not give.

levels.name: Bio Digester content
levels.description: What is in the tank, m3. It fills to the working volume and then passes through what it is fed.

levels.name: Bio Gas holder
levels.description: Biogas in store, Nm3, with its methane share tracked as a component: every inflow carries its own share and every outflow draws the holder's blend, so methane is conserved exactly.

levels.name: Bio Digestate store
levels.description: Digestate waiting for a spreading window, m3. Spilled is overflow: the store filled while spreading was closed.

flows.name: Bio Feeding
flows.description: The feeder, drawing the daily recipe out of the store. Its rate reads the feeder unit's availability, so a breakdown stops the feed for exactly the repair time.

flows.name: Bio Storage loss
flows.description: Losses in store, proportional to what is in store.

flows.name: Bio Feed volume
flows.description: What the feeder delivered, as VOLUME on the site bus -- the digester's inflow and the denominator of its retention time.

flows.name: Bio VS load
flows.description: Organic load delivered, kg of volatile solids per hour, on the site bus -- the numerator of the digester's loading rate.

flows.name: Bio Biogas
flows.description: Gas released by this feedstock, days after it was fed, on its own yield curve. It is posted on the bus; the gas holder takes the total in.

flows.name: Bio CH4
flows.description: The methane inside that gas, on the bus, so the holder can blend several feed lines correctly.

flows.name: Bio Digester in
flows.description: Everything the feed lines on this circuit delivered, as volume.

flows.name: Bio Gas mass out
flows.description: Mass leaving the tank with the gas -- the documented mass-coupling pattern that keeps the balance closed.

flows.name: Bio Digestate out
flows.description: Overflow. A vessel that has reached its working volume passes through what comes in, less the mass that left with the gas -- which is the constant-volume (CSTR) assumption, and is exact: the level does not move, so there is no feedback loop to oscillate. A vessel started part full simply fills until it gets there, and the threshold on the level makes that instant exact.
flows.rate: max(FLOW("$Bio Digester in") - FLOW("$Bio Gas mass out"), 0) * (1 if LEVEL("$Bio Digester content") >= working_volume * 0.99 else 0)

flows.name: Bio Digester heat
flows.description: Process heating asked of the heat bus, kW th.

flows.name: Bio Digester mixing
flows.description: Mixer load on the site electricity bus, kW.

flows.name: Bio OLR
flows.description: Organic loading rate, kg VS per m3 of working volume per day. Its Avg Rate is the KPI and its Starts count how often the design limit was crossed upwards.

flows.name: Bio HRT
flows.description: Hydraulic retention time in days, instantaneous: working volume over the volume fed per day. Its Avg Rate is the time-averaged retention time, capped at 999 days while nothing is being fed.

flows.name: Bio Residual gas
flows.description: Gas still released by the material that has left the tank -- what makes this asset a post-digester. Zero when the residual yield is 0.

flows.name: Bio Residual CH4
flows.description: The methane inside the residual gas, for the holder's blend.

flows.name: Bio Gas in
flows.description: Everything posted as biogas on this circuit, with the blended methane share of what is arriving right now.

flows.name: Bio Gas out
flows.description: Gas served to the consumers. When the holder runs empty the engine scales it down, and the consumers see exactly that through the supply tag.

flows.name: Bio CH4 out
flows.description: The methane inside the served gas, so every consumer reads the same blend without naming this holder.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Gas out") * FRACTION("$Bio Gas holder", "ch4")

flows.name: Bio Flare
flows.description: The flare. It lights on the upper threshold, burns exactly the surplus so the holder holds there, and goes out on the lower one.
flows.rate: min(flare_capacity, max(FLOWSUM("biogas" + circuit) - FLOWSUM("bio_gas_demand" + circuit), 0)) * (1 if VAR("$bio_flare_gate") > capacity * (flare_start_level + flare_stop_level) / 200 else 0)

flows.name: Bio Flare slip
flows.description: Methane that leaves the flare unburned, charged at the methane GWP factor.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Flare") * FRACTION("$Bio Gas holder", "ch4") * flare_ch4_slip / 100

flows.name: Bio Flare combustion
flows.description: Methane the flare burned. Its impact factor is 0 by default: the carbon is biogenic.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Flare") * FRACTION("$Bio Gas holder", "ch4") * (1 - flare_ch4_slip / 100)

flows.name: Bio CHP gas demand
flows.description: Gas the engine asks the holder for, at its rated output and the design methane share. It is 0 while the engine is unavailable or the dispatch rule says stand down, and it is semi-continuous below the minimum load.
flows.rate: AVAILABLE("$Bio CHP engine") * electrical_kw / (electrical_efficiency * ch4_lhv * (max(design_ch4_share, min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)))) * (1 if dispatch == "always" else (1 if TS(electricity_price) * electrical_efficiency * ch4_lhv > biomethane_value else 0))

flows.name: Bio CHP gas burned
flows.description: What the engine actually got: its own demand, capped by what the holder served after the units ahead of it took their share.
flows.rate: max(min(FLOW("$Bio CHP gas demand"), FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit) - FLOWSUM("bio_gas_demand" + circuit, merit)), 0)

flows.name: Bio CHP electricity
flows.description: Electrical output on the site bus, kW: the methane actually burned times its heating value times the electrical efficiency. A negative price is revenue.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio CHP gas burned") * (min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)) * ch4_lhv * electrical_efficiency

flows.name: Bio CHP heat
flows.description: Recoverable heat on the heat bus, kW th.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio CHP gas burned") * (min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)) * ch4_lhv * thermal_efficiency

flows.name: Bio CHP operating cost
flows.description: Service and consumables, priced per kWh generated.

flows.name: Bio Upgrading gas demand
flows.description: Raw gas the unit asks the holder for.
flows.rate: AVAILABLE("$Bio Upgrading skid") * capacity_nm3_h * (1 if dispatch == "always" else (1 if biomethane_value > TS(electricity_price) * chp_efficiency * ch4_lhv else 0))

flows.name: Bio Upgrading gas in
flows.description: Raw gas actually treated: its own demand, capped by what the holder served after the units ahead of it took their share.
flows.rate: max(min(FLOW("$Bio Upgrading gas demand"), FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit) - FLOWSUM("bio_gas_demand" + circuit, merit)), 0)

flows.name: Bio Biomethane
flows.description: Biomethane produced, Nm3 of methane per hour, on the site bus. The Grid injection asset takes it.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Upgrading gas in") * (min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)) * methane_recovery / 100

flows.name: Bio Upgrading slip
flows.description: Methane vented with the off-gas, charged at the methane GWP factor.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Upgrading gas in") * (min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)) * (1 - methane_recovery / 100)

flows.name: Bio Upgrading power
flows.description: Electrical load of the unit on the site bus, kW.

flows.name: Bio Upgrading operating cost
flows.description: Consumables and service, per cubic metre of raw gas treated.

flows.name: Bio Injection
flows.description: Biomethane injected, Nm3 of methane per hour. A negative price is revenue.

flows.name: Bio Curtailed biomethane
flows.description: Biomethane the connection could not take. A non-zero total here says the injection capacity, not the upgrading unit, is the binding constraint.

flows.name: Bio Heat served
flows.description: Process heat actually covered by the CHP and the boiler, kW th.

flows.name: Bio Heat surplus
flows.description: Heat the site cannot use, kW th. A heat-offtake business case starts here.

flows.name: Bio Boiler gas demand
flows.description: Gas the boiler asks the holder for, sized on the heat still missing after the CHP. Its merit number keeps it behind the engines.
flows.rate: min(boiler_capacity_kw, max(FLOWSUM("heat_demand") - FLOWSUM("heat_supply", boiler_merit), 0)) / (boiler_efficiency * ch4_lhv * (max(design_ch4_share, min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0))))

flows.name: Bio Boiler gas burned
flows.description: What the boiler actually got from the holder.
flows.rate: max(min(FLOW("$Bio Boiler gas demand"), FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit) - FLOWSUM("bio_gas_demand" + circuit, boiler_merit)), 0)

flows.name: Bio Boiler heat
flows.description: Boiler output on the heat bus, kW th.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Bio Boiler gas burned") * (min(FLOWSUM("bio_ch4_supply" + circuit) / max(FLOWSUM("bio_gas_supply" + circuit), 1e-9), 1.0)) * ch4_lhv * boiler_efficiency

flows.name: Bio Heat bought
flows.description: Heat bought in because neither the CHP nor the boiler could cover the demand, kW th.

flows.name: Bio Digestate in
flows.description: Digestate arriving from the vessels on this circuit.

flows.name: Bio Spreading out
flows.description: Digestate leaving to the fields, only while a window is open.

flows.name: Nrg load
flows.description: Site demand drawn from the bus, kW.

flows.name: Nrg import
flows.description: Whatever the site could not cover itself, up to the connection limit, kW.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable"), 0), import_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg unserved
flows.description: Demand the connection limit could not deliver, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOW("$Nrg import"), 0)

flows.name: Nrg export
flows.description: Surplus sold to the grid, up to the export limit, kW. A negative price is revenue.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in"), 0), export_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg curtailed
flows.description: Generation that was neither used, stored nor exported, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOW("$Nrg export"), 0)

conversions.name: Bio Yield
conversions.description: Feed in, biogas out over the following days on this feedstock's release curve. Cohorts close hourly.

conversions.name: Bio Residual
conversions.description: Residual gas from the digestate leaving the vessel.

fixed_costs.name: Bio CHP capital
fixed_costs.description: Capital cost of the engine, annualised and prorated over the run.

fixed_costs.name: Bio Upgrading capital
fixed_costs.description: Capital cost of the upgrading plant, annualised and prorated.

info.description: Trucks bringing feedstock onto the site. Each arrival carries a load in entity.bio_load, is charged at the purchase price per tonne, and leaves by the "trucks" port -- chain it to a Feed line, whose store the truck unloads into (it waits if the store is full, so a clamp that is too small shows up as a queue of trucks). Arrivals are either an interval or a seasonal SCHEDULE, which is how an autumn maize campaign is modelled: a schedule with a high rate for eight weeks and zero for the rest of the year. No input port -- this asset starts the flow.

parameters.name: arrival_mode
parameters.label: Arrivals
parameters.help: Interarrival: a truck every "time between trucks". Schedule: a non-homogeneous arrival schedule, which is how a seasonal campaign is written -- trucks only during the harvest weeks.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.label: Time between trucks
parameters.help: Used by Interarrival arrivals only.

parameters.name: schedule
parameters.label: Delivery schedule
parameters.help: Used by Schedule arrivals only. Edit its points in the model's Schedules tab: the shipped one is an autumn campaign -- eight weeks of trucks, then nothing.

parameters.name: tonnes_per_truck
parameters.label: Load per truck
parameters.help: Tonnes for a solid feedstock, cubic metres for a liquid one -- the same unit the Feed line it unloads into uses.

parameters.name: unload_time
parameters.label: Unloading time
parameters.help: Time on site before the truck leaves. It does not hold the store: the load is put in the store at arrival.

parameters.name: price_per_tonne
parameters.label: Purchase price
parameters.help: Charged per tonne delivered, as a per-event cost itemised in the cost summary. 0 for a feedstock that costs nothing at the gate (own slurry); a gate FEE is a negative price.

info.description: One feedstock, end to end: its store, its feeder and its gas yield curve. Trucks arriving at the "deliveries" port unload into the store (they WAIT if it is full, so an undersized clamp shows as a truck queue). The feeder draws the daily recipe out of the store -- stopped for exactly the downtime whenever its own feeder unit fails -- and what it draws is posted on the site bus as volume ("bio_feed") and as organic load ("bio_vs"), which is what the digester integrates into its retention time and loading rate. The same tonnes drive a delayed conversion: the gas comes out over the following days on this feedstock's own yield curve, and is posted as "biogas" with its methane share as "bio_ch4" for the gas holder to blend. Place one Feed line per feedstock; pick the feedstock from the catalogue and the six yield parameters fill in. Store shortfall is the store's own Unmet.

parameters.name: gas_yield
parameters.label: Biogas yield
parameters.help: Cubic metres of biogas per tonne of FRESH matter fed. Pick a feedstock from the catalogue to fill this and the five below.

parameters.name: ch4_share
parameters.label: Methane share
parameters.help: Methane fraction of this feedstock's gas, 0..1. It is carried through the holder as a tracked component, so a mixed feed gives a mixed holder.

parameters.name: half_life_days
parameters.label: Release half-life
parameters.help: How fast the gas comes out: half of the remaining yield every half-life. A readily degradable feedstock is 1-2 days, a fibrous one 4-6.

parameters.name: dry_matter_percent
parameters.label: Dry matter
parameters.help: Used for the organic loading rate only.

parameters.name: volatile_solids_percent
parameters.label: Volatile solids
parameters.help: Share of the dry matter that is organic. Loading rate = fed x DM x VS.

parameters.name: bulk_density
parameters.label: Bulk density
parameters.help: Converts the mass fed into the volume the digester sees, which is what its retention time is computed on. 1.0 for a liquid.

parameters.name: release_steps
parameters.label: Curve steps
parameters.help: Steps the half-life curve is cut into. More steps is a smoother release and slightly more work; 12 is plenty.

parameters.name: store_capacity
parameters.label: Store capacity
parameters.help: The clamp or the tank. A delivery that does not fit waits at the gate.

parameters.name: load_from_truck
parameters.label: Load size from the truck
parameters.help: On: each arrival unloads its own entity.bio_load, which is what the Feedstock delivery asset stamps. Off: every arrival unloads the fixed amount below, which is how any other source of entities can feed the store.

parameters.name: unload_amount
parameters.label: Fixed load size
parameters.help: Used only when the load size does not come from the truck.

parameters.name: storage_loss_percent_month
parameters.label: Storage loss
parameters.help: Losses in store -- silage respiration, effluent -- as a percentage of what is in store, per 30 days. It is modelled as a flow whose rate reads the level, which is EXACT at every event and held constant between them; the hourly re-evaluation of a running model makes the error negligible.

parameters.name: feed_rate
parameters.label: Daily recipe
parameters.help: How much of THIS feedstock goes in per day. The digester's recipe is simply the set of Feed lines you place.

parameters.name: feed_profile
parameters.label: Feeding profile
parameters.help: A multiplier on the recipe by hour of the day. "Bio feed continuous" is a flat 1. "Bio feed 8 batches" is 3.0 for eight hours and 0 for sixteen -- a batch feeder. Any profile you write must AVERAGE 1 over the day, or the daily amount stops being the recipe.

parameters.name: feeder_mtbf
parameters.label: Feeder MTBF
parameters.help: Mean time between feeder failures. The feed stops for exactly the repair time -- the rate reads the feeder's own availability.

parameters.name: initial_feed_rate
parameters.label: Steady-state start
parameters.help: Start the conversion already in the steady state for this feed rate, so a year-long study has no start-up transient to wait out. Set it to the daily recipe; 0 starts from an empty digester.

parameters.name: circuit
parameters.label: Circuit
parameters.help: Leave empty. A site with TWO independent trains (two digesters, two gas holders) gives each train its own circuit name -- ' 2', say -- and every asset of that train carries the same one. It is appended to this asset's bus tags, so the two trains never mix. Electricity, heat and biomethane are site-wide and are never circuited.

info.description: The vessel. It takes whatever the Feed lines on its circuit post, holds it at its working volume, and pushes the rest out as digestate. It reports the two numbers a digester is designed on: the hydraulic retention time (working volume over the volume fed per day) and the organic loading rate (kg of volatile solids per cubic metre per day), each as a flow whose Avg Rate is the KPI, with a rising threshold on the loading rate that counts how often the design limit was passed. It asks the heat bus for its heating and the electricity bus for its mixers, so an Energy-library Grid connection sees them. Place a SECOND one as a post-digester: set its inlet to the first one's outlet, give it a residual yield, and the gas it still makes joins the same holder. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.name: working_volume
parameters.label: Working volume
parameters.help: The liquid volume. Retention time and loading rate are both computed on it.

parameters.name: initial_fill
parameters.label: Fill at the start
parameters.help: Fraction of the working volume in the tank at t=0. 0.99 is the operating point: the vessel is full and what comes in goes out.

parameters.name: gas_density
parameters.label: Gas density
parameters.help: Mass the gas carries out of the tank, per cubic metre of biogas. About 1.2 kg/Nm3; it closes the mass balance and is small.

parameters.name: heat_per_m3
parameters.label: Heating demand
parameters.help: Heat to hold the process temperature, per cubic metre of working volume. It is posted on the heat bus as demand; place a Heat balance to serve it.

parameters.name: mixing_kw
parameters.label: Mixing power
parameters.help: Electrical load of the mixers, posted on the site electricity bus under "demand" -- the same tag the Energy library's assets use.

parameters.name: residual_yield
parameters.label: Residual gas yield
parameters.help: Gas still to come out of the material LEAVING this vessel, per cubic metre. 0 for a main digester whose Feed lines already carry the whole yield; a post-digester is this asset with a residual yield of a few Nm3/m3.

parameters.name: max_olr
parameters.label: Loading rate limit
parameters.help: The design limit. Crossing it upwards is counted as the loading-rate flow's Starts, so the run reports how often the digester was overloaded. It is a WARNING, not a constraint: the engine does not stop the feed.

parameters.name: circuit
parameters.label: Circuit
parameters.help: Leave empty. A site with TWO independent trains (two digesters, two gas holders) gives each train its own circuit name -- ' 2', say -- and every asset of that train carries the same one. It is appended to this asset's bus tags, so the two trains never mix. Electricity, heat and biomethane are site-wide and are never circuited.

parameters.name: inlet_tag
parameters.label: Inlet
parameters.help: The bus tag this vessel takes its inflow from. "bio_feed" is what the Feed lines post. A post-digester takes "digestate" -- the outlet of the vessel before it.

parameters.name: outlet_tag
parameters.label: Outlet
parameters.help: The bus tag its overflow is posted under. The Digestate store reads it. Two vessels in series need different outlets: "digestate" then "digestate_final".

parameters.name: vs_tag
parameters.label: Organic load inlet
parameters.help: Where the loading rate is read from. Leave it for a main digester; a post-digester has no fresh organic load, so point it at a tag nobody posts ("none") and its loading rate reads 0.

parameters.name: working_volume
parameters.description: The liquid volume. Retention time and loading rate are both computed on it.

parameters.name: initial_fill
parameters.description: Fraction of the working volume in the tank at t=0. 0.99 is the operating point: the vessel is full and what comes in goes out.

parameters.name: gas_density
parameters.description: Mass the gas carries out of the tank, per cubic metre of biogas. About 1.2 kg/Nm3; it closes the mass balance and is small.

parameters.name: heat_per_m3
parameters.description: Heat to hold the process temperature, per cubic metre of working volume. It is posted on the heat bus as demand; place a Heat balance to serve it.

parameters.name: mixing_kw
parameters.description: Electrical load of the mixers, posted on the site electricity bus under "demand" -- the same tag the Energy library's assets use.

parameters.name: residual_yield
parameters.description: Gas still to come out of the material LEAVING this vessel, per cubic metre. 0 for a main digester whose Feed lines already carry the whole yield; a post-digester is this asset with a residual yield of a few Nm3/m3.

info.description: The buffer between the digesters and everything that burns gas. It takes the whole "biogas" tag in, tracks the methane as a component (so a mixed feed gives a mixed holder and the methane is conserved exactly), and serves whatever the CHP, the upgrading unit and the boiler ask for -- in merit order, because each of them only takes what the units ahead of it left. Its flare opens on a hysteresis band (two level thresholds writing this holder's OWN gate variable) and burns exactly the surplus, so the holder holds at the upper threshold instead of chattering. Flare methane slip is a parameter with its own GWP factor; the CO2 from burning biogenic gas is NOT counted by default, which is what the 0 impact factor means -- change it if your accounting says otherwise. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.name: flare_capacity
parameters.label: Flare capacity
parameters.help: The most the flare can burn. A surplus bigger than this pushes the holder to its capacity, and what will not fit is reported as the holder's Spilled -- gas through the pressure relief, which a well-sized plant never has.

parameters.name: flare_start_level
parameters.label: Flare starts at
parameters.help: Percentage of the holder capacity at which the flare lights.

parameters.name: flare_stop_level
parameters.label: Flare stops at
parameters.help: And at which it goes out again. The gap between the two is the hysteresis band -- it is what stops the flare switching on and off continuously.

parameters.name: flare_ch4_slip
parameters.label: Flare methane slip
parameters.help: Share of the methane sent to the flare that leaves unburned. It is charged at the methane GWP factor below.

parameters.name: slip_impact_factor
parameters.label: Methane GWP factor
parameters.help: Impact of one cubic metre of methane released. About 0.72 kg of methane per Nm3 at a 100-year GWP near 28.

parameters.name: flare_impact_factor
parameters.label: Flared CO2 factor
parameters.help: Impact of the methane the flare actually BURNS. It defaults to 0 because that carbon is biogenic -- it came out of the crop this year. Set it to about 1.96 if your accounting counts biogenic CO2.

info.description: A gas engine on the holder. It asks the holder for the gas its rated output needs, takes what the units ahead of it in the merit order left, and turns the methane in it into electricity (tagged "generation", the same tag the Energy library uses, so an Energy-library Grid connection balances the site) and heat (tagged "heat_supply", which the Heat balance serves the digester from). It stops for exactly the downtime of its own maintenance schedule and its own random failures, is semi-continuous below its minimum load, and is charged a start cost every time it restarts. Its capital cost is an annualised fixed cost prorated over the run, so a sizing run over the rated power compares like with like. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.name: min_load_percent
parameters.label: Minimum load
parameters.help: Below this the engine is OFF, not part-loaded. It is a semi-continuous gate on the gas it asks for.

parameters.name: merit
parameters.label: Merit order
parameters.help: Order on the gas holder: 1 is served first. Give the upgrading unit a higher number for "CHP first", a lower one for "biomethane first".

parameters.name: ch4_lhv
parameters.label: Methane heating value
parameters.help: Lower heating value of methane. 9.97 kWh per normal cubic metre is the standard figure; it is a parameter so a different reference state can be used.

parameters.name: design_ch4_share
parameters.label: Design methane share
parameters.help: The methane share the gas valve is set for. It sizes how much gas the engine ASKS for -- and a RICHER gas than this makes it ask for proportionally less, so the engine never exceeds its rating. A leaner gas than this simply gives less power.

parameters.name: maintenance_schedule
parameters.label: Maintenance schedule
parameters.help: A capacity schedule on the engine: 1 while it is available, 0 during planned service. The shipped one is 30 days up, 1 day down.

parameters.name: mtbf
parameters.label: MTBF
parameters.help: Unplanned failures, on top of the schedule.

parameters.name: dispatch
parameters.label: Dispatch rule
parameters.help: always: run whenever gas is there. when_better_than_biomethane: run only while a cubic metre of methane is worth more as electricity (price x electrical efficiency x heating value) than as biomethane. Set the upgrading unit to the mirror rule and the gas follows the price.

parameters.name: electricity_price
parameters.label: Electricity price
parameters.help: EUR/kWh by hour. It both prices the output and decides the price-led dispatch.

parameters.name: biomethane_value
parameters.label: Biomethane value
parameters.help: What a cubic metre of methane is worth if it were upgraded instead. Used by the price-led rule only.

parameters.name: sell_electricity
parameters.label: Sell the electricity
parameters.help: On: the output is sold at the price profile and shows as revenue. Turn it OFF if you place an Energy-library Grid connection, which prices the export itself -- otherwise the revenue is counted twice.

parameters.name: om_per_kwh
parameters.label: Operating cost
parameters.help: Service contract and consumables, per kWh generated.

parameters.name: start_cost
parameters.label: Start cost
parameters.help: Charged every time the engine restarts. Starts are counted as the gas flow's Starts.

parameters.name: capex_per_kw
parameters.label: Capital cost
parameters.help: Installed cost per kW of rating. It is per kW, not a lump, so a sizing run over the rated power prices the engine it is actually asking for.

parameters.name: annual_cost_rate
parameters.label: Annual cost rate
parameters.help: Fraction of the capital cost charged per year -- depreciation plus cost of capital. The charge is PRORATED over the run (amount x HORIZON / 8760), so capex and operating cost cover the same window. 0 leaves it out.

info.description: Raw biogas in, biomethane out. It asks the holder for gas up to its rated throughput, takes what the units ahead of it in the merit order left, recovers the stated share of the methane and vents the rest -- which is charged at the methane GWP factor, because a slipped cubic metre is the single biggest emission an upgrading plant has. Its electricity use goes on the site bus under "demand", the same tag the Energy library reads. Pick the technology from the catalogue and the recovery, the electricity use and the capital cost fill in. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

info.description: The meter at the gas grid. It injects whatever the upgrading units produced, up to the connection capacity, and books the revenue -- price plus incentive, both per cubic metre of methane, optionally shaped by a price profile. Anything over the capacity is CURTAILED and reported separately, which is the number that tells you whether the connection or the upgrading unit is the binding constraint. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.help: The grid connection's limit, in cubic metres of methane per hour.

parameters.label: Incentive

parameters.name: price_profile
parameters.label: Price profile
parameters.help: A MULTIPLIER on the commodity price, by hour. The shipped profile is a flat 1.0, which is the constant-price case; replace its values for a seasonal or indexed price. The incentive is never scaled.

info.description: Closes the heat side. Whatever the digesters ask for on "heat_demand" is served first from the CHP heat on "heat_supply"; what is missing is made by a gas boiler on the holder (last in the merit order by default, so it only gets gas nobody else wanted), and anything the boiler still cannot cover is bought in at a price -- which is the honest way to show that a plant without enough CHP heat has a bill, not a miracle. Heat the site cannot use is reported as surplus, which is the number a heat-offtake business case starts from. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

info.description: The lagoon. It takes the digestate the digesters push out and empties only during the spreading windows -- a 0/1 profile over the year, which is what a nitrate regulation actually is. The store has to carry the whole closed period, so this is a real sizing constraint: if it fills before the window opens, the overflow shows up as the level's Spilled and the plant has a problem. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

info.description: The meter: whatever the site cannot cover itself is imported and priced on a tariff profile, whatever it cannot use or store is exported up to the export limit, and the rest is curtailed. Import beyond the import limit is recorded as unserved demand rather than silently supplied. Emissions follow a grid intensity profile, so a sustainability assessment is the same run. Place exactly one per site: it is the slack that closes the energy balance. No ports: this is a continuous asset. A demand charge on the peak import power is billed once at the end of the run.

parameters.name: import_profile
parameters.label: Import tariff
parameters.help: Import price by hour of the day, EUR/kWh. A flat tariff is a one-value profile.

parameters.name: export_price
parameters.label: Export price
parameters.help: Paid for every exported kWh: it enters Total Cost as a negative cost.

parameters.name: intensity_profile
parameters.label: Grid carbon intensity
parameters.help: kg CO2e per imported kWh, by hour of the day. It drives Total Impact, which is deliberately generic: use it for water, waste or any other per-unit impact instead.

parameters.name: import_limit_kw
parameters.label: Import limit
parameters.help: Connection capacity. Demand beyond it is recorded as unserved energy, not supplied.

parameters.name: export_limit_kw
parameters.label: Export limit
parameters.help: Largest power the meter may export. Surplus beyond it is curtailed, which the curtailment flow accounts for.

parameters.name: demand_charge_per_kw
parameters.label: Demand charge
parameters.help: Billed once on the highest import power the site actually HELD (the import flow's Peak Rate), the way a network operator bills capacity. 0 for an energy-only tariff.

parameters.description: Connection capacity. Demand beyond it is recorded as unserved energy, not supplied.

parameters.name: export_limit_kw
parameters.description: Largest power the meter may export. Surplus beyond it is curtailed, which the curtailment flow accounts for.

parameters.name: demand_charge_per_kw
parameters.description: Billed once on the highest import power the site actually HELD (the import flow's Peak Rate), the way a network operator bills capacity. 0 for an energy-only tariff.

info.title: Biogas plant (library assets)
info.description: A farm-scale biogas plant built ONLY from library assets: two feedstock deliveries (an autumn maize campaign and slurry tankers all year) into two feed lines, a 4000 m3 digester and a 2000 m3 post-digester, a 1500 Nm3 gas holder with a flare, a 500 kW CHP unit and a 120 Nm3/h membrane upgrading plant sharing the gas in merit order, grid injection, the heat balance, a 12 000 m3 digestate store on seasonal spreading windows, and the Energy library's site load and grid connection on the same electricity bus. Nothing is wired except the two truck links: everything continuous meets on the site bus. Base unit hours, one simulated YEAR of REAL DATES from the maize harvest on Monday 7 September 2026 (Europe/Rome): the campaign is a weekday delivery pattern that a dated exception closes when the harvest ends, the spreading windows are dated weeks, and the power price repeats "weekly" in calendar terms.
info.author: Naga
info.notes: Total Cost is the annual margin, negated: feedstock purchases, CHP and upgrading operating cost and annualised capex, CHP starts, bought heat and grid import, less the electricity and biomethane revenue. That makes it the objective a sizing run minimises: naga optimize --factor blocks.<holder>.params.arguments.capacity --factor blocks.<upgrading>.params.arguments.capacity_nm3_h --factor blocks.<chp>.params.arguments.electrical_kw --response system/Total Cost --goal min. The CHP sells its own output at the hourly price series and the grid connection's export price is 0, so the electricity revenue is booked once. Both the price series and the spreading windows are SYNTHETIC. Total Impact is the methane slipped by the flare and the upgrading unit plus the grid import's carbon intensity; biogenic CO2 is not counted.
